source.repro: node plugins/linear-comparative-view/benches/culledRibbonMates.bench.ts - min of 15 rounds, three instances per feature.
source.notes:
The class the WORKER cannot see: the mate is on a contig the facing row displays and has scrolled off, so whether it is a mark is a question about the current transform (see agent-docs/ideas/offscreen-synteny-mates.md). 1500px band, 100px tall. Every query span inside one 2Mb window at 2000bp/px, so every mark lands on screen and none is rejected before the walk; mates spread over a 500Mb genome by a coprime stride, which is what a facing row can scroll clear of. The fill is a no-op, so no column here measures rasterization.

WHAT IT SAYS. `repaint` and `control` are the SAME within noise at every size, and control is the identical dataset with the mate lane removed - which is exactly what a class A strip of that mark count costs. So the per-entry band test is free, and the repaint column is the rect-per-mark cost both classes already had (offscreen-mate-overlay.json is the same shape measured on the same code). What this change adds is that the ceiling is now reachable in a state that previously drew nothing at all: query row zoomed out, facing row zoomed in.

`covered` is the state a reader is in most of the time - a facing row whose band spans every mate the fetch holds - and it is the whole justification for carrying the extent on `mateAxis`: two comparisons drop the dataset out of the lane, turning a 15ms walk at 100k into 0.000ms.

`build` is the only genuinely new work, once per fetch, on a setting that is on by default, and it now resolves BOTH rows' perspectives rather than the query row's alone - the second one is what marks a ribbon the row above scrolled off, on the axis it still has. Interleaved A/B in one process against the one-perspective version, 25 rounds: 0.35 -> 0.39ms at 10k features, 3.51 -> 3.84ms at 100k, 18.90 -> 19.96ms at 500k. About 6%, for one more Uint32Array per fetch and one more per-feature increment; the instance walk, which is the pass, is unchanged.

`hover` is a pointer over the ribbons below the strip, unchanged because the strip height is still tested before any alignment is.

Re-measured whole on 2026-08-25 rather than patched: the 2026-08-23 run was on the same bench and the same machine but is systematically slower across every column, so its rows and these cannot be compared cell by cell. The A/B above is the comparison that holds, because both arms ran in one process on one dataset.
